anchors.raw: I want to keep going at the gym, because there is a good group, and so, and I would like to see if I can squeeze like three session training with you, and like two at the gym
anchors.note: He intends to keep paying for and attending his existing gym, so the programme is priced as an addition to a cost he is already carrying rather than a replacement for it. The rep never surfaced or repositioned this.

anchors.raw: I think those two things are really... It's for me because I'm not rich. don't know how much it can cost generally.
anchors.note: He told the rep before the number was given that he had no price frame and self-identified as not wealthy. That was the cue to build value and pre-frame; instead the number arrived two turns later with nothing under it.

unmet_demand.want: To run the programme alongside his existing gym training — roughly three coached sessions plus two gym sessions a week — and to know whether that is compatible
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked this directly in his opening answer and it was never answered anywhere on the call. Nothing in the transcript establishes whether the programme accommodates concurrent outside training.

unmet_demand.want: Daily, hands-on coaching contact rather than a programme sent to him — 'I want someone that can really help me day by day. It's not just sending me the stuff'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The accountability pillar, which is presumably the answer to this, was never presented. The prospect's central purchase criterion went unaddressed.

unmet_demand.want: A way to measure and progress flexibility, including loaded/active work rather than passive stretching — 'I don't have a real progression because I don't know how to measure it'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep acknowledged the problem ('I know what you mean') but never described how the programme progresses or measures mobility.
